title: Scheme-test pullbacks of maps from coproduct schemes to coproduct sheaves
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], fix its big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] with the size convention [def-weil-size-convention], and let $I$ be a small set in that convention. Let $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ be sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $C=\coprod_iG_i$ be their coproduct in sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and write $c_i:G_i\to C$ for the coprojections. For a scheme $X$ over $S$, write $h_X(Z)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(Z,X)$. Let $U_i$ be schemes over $S$, let $p_i:h_{U_i}\to G_i$ be natural transformations, and assume the scheme coproduct $U=\coprod_iU_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] is an object of the fixed site, with inclusions $\iota_i:U_i\to U$. Let $p:h_U\to C$ be a natural transformation whose restriction to $h_{U_i}$ is $c_ip_i$. Let $T$ be a site object and $a\in C(T)$. Suppose $T=\coprod_iT_i$ is a clopen partition with sections $a_i\in G_i(T_i)$ satisfying $c_i(a_i)=a|_{T_i}$; a clopen partition is a pairwise disjoint open covering with the open subscheme structures [def-weil-open-immersion]. Suppose for each $i$ the sheaf fibre product $h_{T_i}\times_{G_i}h_{U_i}$ is represented by a scheme $V_i$, with projections $q_i:V_i\to T_i$ and $r_i:V_i\to U_i$ (representability as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]). Then $V=\coprod_iV_i$ represents $h_T\times_Ch_U$: for every site object $Z$ there is a bijection $$\operatorname{Mor}_S(Z,V)\ \cong\ \{(f,u)\mid f:Z\to T,\ u:Z\to U,\ a f=p u\},$$ natural in $Z$. Under this bijection the projections $V\to T$ and $V\to U$ restrict on $V_i$ to $q_i$ followed by $T_i\to T$ and to $\iota_ir_i$, respectively. For each pair $(f,u)$ on the right, $u^{-1}(U_i)=f^{-1}(T_i)$ as open subschemes of $Z$. Empty index sets and empty summands are allowed. Neither algebraic-space hypotheses on $G_i$ nor etaleness or surjectivity of $p_i$ are assumed.

proof.text: First derive open immersions, joint surjectivity and disjointness for any specified scheme coproduct, without requiring its entire index type to be small. For open immersions, send the chosen summand into the left side of X_i coproduct Y and all other summands into the right side; the original inclusion is a pullback of the left inclusion. Joint surjectivity follows by factoring the identity through the union of the image opens; disjointness follows by mapping two different labels into different sides of Y coproduct Y. The set of indices of nonempty V_i injects into T by choosing a point, mapping through q_i and using disjointness of d.opens. It is therefore small in the scheme universe. Form its actual Mathlib scheme coproduct, insert the omitted empty schemes using their initiality, and prove the full coproduct universal property. Descend the structure maps to S and then the maps Q and R, obtaining the two prescribed restriction equations.

proof.text: Use the cartesian-square conclusion of the existing fppf coproduct partition theorem. For the section corresponding to p on Ucop, it gives a partition D and cartesian summand squares. The given restrictions hp give maps U_i into the corresponding D_i. Because the U_i cover Ucop and distinct D_i are disjoint, the image of U_i is exactly D_i. The open-immersion comparison is an isomorphism, so transport the partition square to obtain the cartesian square with U_i, p_i, p and c_i. For any compatible test pair (f,b), lift on the inverse image of U_i through the partition square for d; this proves b inverse-image U_i is contained in f inverse-image T_i. Reverse the two cartesian squares to obtain the opposite containment, hence equality of these open subschemes.

source.place: Tag 02WQ (lemma-coproduct-algebraic-spaces), the scheme-test comparison underlying the resulting map from the coproduct atlas; Tag 0F15 (lemma-coproduct-sheaves-open-and-closed) and Tag 02WO (lemma-representable-sheaf-coproduct-sheaves).

proof.text: The component squares and the partition squares imply commutativity of Q and R on every V_i. Their inclusions form an open cover, hence an fppf covering; the separatedness axiom of C gives commutativity globally. Given a compatible pair (f,b), the inverse images of U_i form a disjoint open covering of Z. Its scheme coproduct cofan is colimiting, by gluing morphisms and using initiality of the empty overlaps. On each piece first lift through the cartesian square for T_i, and then through the assumed component square for V_i. Compose these local lifts with V_i into Vcop and descend along this cofan. Coproduct uniqueness and the local equations show its projections are f and b.

source.place: Tag 02WQ (lemma-coproduct-algebraic-spaces), the scheme-test comparison underlying the resulting map from the coproduct atlas; Tag 0F15 (lemma-coproduct-sheaves-open-and-closed) and Tag 02WO (lemma-representable-sheaf-coproduct-sheaves).

proof.text: To prove uniqueness, for f,g from Z to Vcop with equal Q and R projections use the partition pulled back from Ucop along f followed by R. The inverse image under R of U_i is exactly the image of V_i: the restriction equation gives one inclusion, and the covering and disjointness of both coproducts give the other. Thus both f and g factor through V_i on the i-th piece. Cancel the open inclusions T_i into T and U_i into Ucop to identify their component projections. The assumed component pullback gives equality of their local maps, and coproduct uniqueness gives f=g.

source.place: Tag 02WQ (lemma-coproduct-algebraic-spaces), the scheme-test comparison underlying the resulting map from the coproduct atlas; Tag 0F15 (lemma-coproduct-sheaves-open-and-closed) and Tag 02WO (lemma-representable-sheaf-coproduct-sheaves).

proof.text: Apply the pointwise pullback criterion in the presheaf category. At each test object, lifted Yoneda identifies sections with maps of schemes over S; the global commutativity, existence and uniqueness just proved are precisely the three conditions for a pullback of sets. Thus the resulting presheaf square is cartesian and natural automatically. Empty indices and empty summands use the same initial-object and cofan arguments; no point is chosen from an empty summand. The inverse-image equality proved above is the final clause.

Step 1: Q and R come from the coproduct mapping property; a_i q_i v = p_i r_i v holds at the site object Z_i (not on V_i); equality on Z follows from the converse/uniqueness clause of lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition. Step 2: the partition of p(id_U) is (U_i) because U is a site object and p|h_{U_i}=c_i p_i; functoriality and uniqueness give u^{-1}(U_i)=f^{-1}(T_i) as open subschemes, and injectivity of c_i gives a_i f_i=p_i u_i. Step 3: lifts at the site objects W_i glue (overlaps are empty and the empty scheme is initial by the I=∅ case of the coproduct node), and gluing uniqueness gives Qv=f and Rv=u. Step 4: the inverse argument is correct; that v|Z_i factors through the open immersion V_i is one line. Step 5: naturality holds, and the cases I=∅ and empty summands are correct. The statement adds no hypothesis, keeps 02WQ's size condition and claims representability only on site objects, which is what the citer lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct Step 4 uses. lean.note: The IsPullback of lifted representables is exactly the natural representing bijection, with both projections specified on each summand.
